decided.claim: A BEL on an agent pane never rings instantly anymore: it parks as a deferred finish-claim that the effects clock announces only after the live screen has held spinner-free for 300ms (the same hold the scan path's not-thinking debounce uses), so every genuine bell announcement is delayed a few ticks by design — the stated trade of delayed-beats-false, and the uniform hold is what stops a beep landing in a redraw flicker from ringing.

Both reported bugs are judged against one new observation clock, last_seen_thinking (when the scroll-proof live-screen probe last SAW the working spinner): a claim parks only if the pane observed its agent working within the last 30s — a restored pane replaying its transcript has observed none, so the replay burst is discarded on arrival — and a parked claim that still sees the spinner when it expires at 10s is dropped, which is the scrollback-beep case; the real finish is then a long spell the scan path announces itself.

Hoisted the agent_is_thinking probe out of the scroll-settle gate in the 120ms tick so the observation clock stays honest mid-scroll (the probe reads the live buffer bottom, so it was already scroll-proof); the settled scan block consumes the identical same-tick probe value, keeping the scan path and all its guards behaviourally unchanged.

A BEL arriving while the finish badge is already latched is ignored (the old arm re-played the sound and re-emitted AgentDone), and the resolver drops any pending claim once the scan latches, so a stale claim can never re-ring after the user acks.

The decision logic is extracted as pure functions — bell_claim_plausible and deferred_bell_outcome with the DeferredBell verdict enum — unit-tested in the existing pane tests module, matching the repo's idiom of pure, testable helpers (wants_human, looks_blocked) around untestable gpui entity wiring.

Added a correctness-matrix test pinning that a raw 0x07 byte emits exactly one Event::Bell without disturbing surrounding text, because the whole claim path (and the transcript-replay failure mode) hangs off that emission surviving crate bumps.

Thresholds: 30s recent-work window (separates just-finished from replayed/idle), 300ms quiet hold (deliberately equal to the scan's existing debounce), 10s claim expiry (past which a bell demonstrably was not a finish); all module constants next to the pure functions.

least_confident.why: The 30s window and 10s expiry are judgment values, not measurements: an agent CLI that rings its bell while its done-screen still matches the spinner phrase ("interrupt)") would have its bell expire and fall back to the scan, and I could not observe real CLIs' bell-vs-redraw ordering without running one.

Deferring EVERY bell (rather than ringing instantly when the screen already reads not-thinking) adds ~300-450ms to all genuine bell announcements; the brief blesses delay over falseness, but if instant bells mattered more than I read, this is the decision to relax.

Suppressing repeat BELs while the badge is latched removes a re-alert behaviour that may have been intentional for back-to-back finishes, though it looked accidental (the old arm simply re-ran unconditionally).

not_done.claim: No build, test, clippy, or rustfmt run — compile-correctness (borrowck, let-else, match ergonomics in the term.rs filter closure, formatting) is verified by reading only.
not_done.why: Builds are out of scope for this exercise per the run rules.

not_done.claim: The TerminalView wiring (BEL arm -> parked claim -> effects-clock resolution -> sound/badge/AgentDone) is untested in isolation; only the pure decision pair and the emulator's Bell emission have tests. The two reported scenarios end-to-end (a real Claude Code beep during scrollback, a real window restore replaying a transcript) need a live PTY and a real agent to exercise.
not_done.why: TerminalView requires a gpui Context, a spawned PTY session, and real time; faking that harness would be a fake verification.

not_done.claim: The screen-scan path and its guards are untouched, including the scroll-settle gate whose comment claims a protection that agent_is_thinking's own comment says is unnecessary (the probe is viewport-independent) — noticed, not changed.
not_done.why: The brief pins the scan path's current behaviour; reconciling the stale comment is cleanup with behavioural risk and belongs to a separate change.

not_done.claim: A replayed or live transcript that literally QUOTES the phrase "esc to interrupt" in its bottom rows can still fool the spinner heuristic (and therefore park, and possibly later ring, a claim).
not_done.why: Inherent to the existing phrase-based agent_is_thinking heuristic that the scan path also relies on; fixing it is out of this ticket's proportion.

not_done.claim: TD_GAMBA_DEMO panes (probe forced to always-thinking) now never ring from a BEL — claims park and expire.
not_done.why: Demo windows show a frozen fake screen with no real agent; an alert there was noise, but it is a behaviour change I did not separately gate.
